headline: Bitcoin steady near $80,500 overnight; ether slips, privacy coins lead
summary: Bitcoin is near $80,500 in quiet overnight trading, roughly flat over 24 hours after Saturday morning's dip to about $79,260 on reports of U.S. staff being pulled from Middle East posts over Iranian threats; ether (about $2,345, down 1.4%) and most large altcoins are slightly lower, while Monero (up about 3%), Zcash (up about 2%) and XRP (up about 1%) lead and NEAR (down about 5%) and the small AKEDO token (down about 9%) lag. Total crypto market value is about $2.72 trillion (down 2.9%), bitcoin's share is 59.5%, and the Fear & Greed index reads 54 (Neutral). Stock markets are closed until Monday after Friday's oil-driven pullback left the S&P 500 at 7,624 (a second weekly loss) and the TSX at 35,788, with the 10-year yield near 4.99% and Wednesday's Fed and Bank of Canada decisions next.

crypto.label: Cautious
crypto.why: Bitcoin is holding about $80,500 overnight and the Fear & Greed index is a neutral 54, but it is still below its 50-day average, ETFs saw about $773 million of outflows Thursday and Friday, and most large altcoins remain a little lower on the day.

stocks.label: Mixed
stocks.why: Chip stocks limited the Nasdaq's losses, but Brent near a six-month high, a 10-year yield near 5%, a VIX near 19.5 and consumer sentiment near a record low (48.0) dragged the Dow, banks and the TSX lower into the weekend.

drivers.title: AI-spending doubts hit Big Tech and chips
drivers.detail: Meta closed down 7% Thursday despite beating forecasts as investors weighed its $135–$145 billion spending plan; AMD, Amazon, Nvidia and Broadcom fell 4–8%. Friday the selling eased, with AMD, Intel (both up 1.7%) and Micron (up 2.5%) bouncing, though Meta, Amazon and Alphabet slipped another 1% ahead of more Big Tech results next week.
drivers.assets: Nasdaq, chip stocks, Shopify, Celestica, bitcoin

drivers.title: Yields climb back to 5%
drivers.detail: After its biggest one-day drop in more than a year Thursday, the 10-year Treasury yield closed Friday near 4.99% as oil revives inflation worries; the University of Michigan survey shows year-ahead inflation expectations up to 4.7%. CME FedWatch data show only about an 8% chance of a Fed hike on Oct. 28, but roughly 84% odds of one by year-end.

drivers.title: Brent hits six-month high on Gulf escalation
drivers.detail: Brent settled up 3.1% at about $116.70, its highest in about six months and up from under $97 at the start of October, and U.S. crude rose about 4% to roughly $103.30, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, Iranian threats against Gulf energy sites and fears that fighting could resume after the U.S. midterms. Saturday, the UAE was still working to contain oil leaking from an unnamed offshore tanker that has closed beaches in Sharjah, Umm Al Quwain and Ras Al Khaimah; no cause has been given, but attacks on Gulf shipping since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran keep traders on edge going into Monday.

drivers.title: SpaceX wireless report hits U.S. telecoms
drivers.detail: AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile slid after Bloomberg reported SpaceX wants access to about 80,000 U.S. cell sites and is talking with tower owners. Verizon is a Dow member, and the telecom drop, together with American Express (down 3.7%), Caterpillar (down 2.4%) and JPMorgan (down 1.5%), helps explain why the Dow, down 1.2%, was the weakest U.S. index.

drivers.title: Bitcoin tests $80,000 as leveraged bets unwind
drivers.detail: Bitcoin dipped to about $79,260 Saturday morning, its first trip below $80,000 since Oct. 15, after the Wall Street Journal reported the U.S. was moving personnel out of Middle East embassies and military bases over intelligence that Iran was preparing attacks, per CoinDesk; about $821 million of leveraged positions (borrowed bets) across crypto were forcibly closed over 24 hours, 84% of them bets on rising prices. It has since recovered to about $80,600, roughly flat on the day, in quiet trading, following about $773 million of spot bitcoin ETF outflows Thursday and Friday.

drivers.title: Bank of Canada rate hike now likely
drivers.detail: Swap markets price about 80% odds of a Bank of Canada hike to 2.50% on Oct. 28 after strong retail sales and Governor Macklem's warning on oil-driven inflation. The loonie rose to 71.46 U.S. cents from 71.32 Thursday, near a one-month high, while RBC and TD each slipped about 0.4%.

crypto.name: Bitcoin
crypto.move: Flat in 24h (down 0.3%) and down 1.5% this week, at about $80,550 (down 4.5% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Bitcoin slipped through $80,000 Saturday morning, its first trip below that level since Oct. 15, and bottomed near $79,260 after the Wall Street Journal reported the U.S. was pulling personnel out of Middle East embassies and military bases over intelligence that Iran was preparing attacks on Americans, per CoinDesk. Liquidations (exchanges automatically closing leveraged bets when losses eat through the trader's deposit) piled up: about $240 million of bitcoin positions were closed over 24 hours, 93% of them bullish bets, per CoinGlass data cited by The Crypto Times. The drop builds on Thursday's AI-spending scare in tech stocks and about $773 million of spot ETF outflows Thursday and Friday. It has since held between about $80,000 and $81,000 in quiet weekend trading, and into early Sunday it sits near $80,600, roughly where it stood 24 hours earlier, but remains below its 50-day average (about $81,800), a line it closed under on Friday for the first time in 66 days.
crypto.meaning: The $80,000 floor of the $80,000–$87,000 range bitcoin held for a month has given way, at least for now, on thin weekend volume. Weekend breaks sometimes reverse when bigger players return Monday, so whether it climbs back above $80,000 quickly matters more than the move itself; some traders had flagged $75,000 as the next area of interest if the floor failed. It is still about 37% above its July 1 low of $57,850.

outlook.bullCase: Holding above $80,000 and then reclaiming $81,800 (the 50-day average) and $82,600 (the 20-day average), helped by ETF inflows returning Monday and a calmer Nasdaq, would make Saturday's dip look like a weekend shake-out and put $84,000–$85,000 back in view.
outlook.bearCase: Slipping back under $80,000, more ETF outflows, or a hawkish Fed on Oct. 28 could extend the slide toward the 100-day average near $75,300, with $70,000 the next level some traders cite.
outlook.watch: Whether bitcoin closes the weekend above or below $80,000, Monday's ETF flow data, oil when futures reopen Sunday evening, the Fed decision on Oct. 28, and about $11.7 billion of bitcoin options expiring Oct. 30.

crypto.name: Ethereum
crypto.move: Down 1.4% in 24h and 2.9% this week, at about $2,345 (down 13% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Ether fell with bitcoin's break below $80,000 Saturday morning, dropping as low as about $2,290 before recovering to about $2,340, after already losing the $2,400 level that had supported it for about a week. Leveraged ether bets were hit almost as hard as bitcoin's (about $188 million liquidated over 24 hours versus $240 million for bitcoin, per CoinGlass data cited by The Crypto Times), even though ether is less than a fifth of bitcoin's size. Ether ETFs saw outflows on 14 of 17 trading days in October, about $1.2 billion in all, and developers on Friday postponed a test of the next big upgrade, Glamsterdam, after security researchers flagged a risk to existing smart contracts, per CoinDesk.
crypto.meaning: Ether is lagging bitcoin because big investors keep pulling money from the ETFs. Until those flows turn, rallies may be harder to sustain.

outlook.bullCase: Climbing back above $2,400, with ETF outflows stopping, could open a move toward $2,500 and then about $2,700, where October began.
outlook.bearCase: Holding below $2,300 with continued ETF outflows and more forced selling could send it toward $2,150–$2,200, and a broader risk-off turn could push it lower.
outlook.watch: Daily ether ETF flows, the $2,300 and $2,400 levels, the ETH/BTC ratio, and any new Glamsterdam upgrade timeline.

crypto.name: XRP
crypto.move: Up 0.9% in 24h and about flat this week, at about $1.30 (down 15% over 30 days)
crypto.why: XRP is one of the few large coins in the green this weekend. CoinDesk reported Saturday that Franklin Templeton on Thursday put about $150 million more of its tokenized money-market fund (sgBENJI, a fund whose shares exist as tokens on a blockchain) onto the XRP Ledger, taking the fund's holdings there to nearly 193 million shares, worth roughly $200 million. All of the new shares sit in a single wallet linked to Franklin's issuing account, and it is not clear whether they belong to one investor or several.
crypto.meaning: A big asset manager using the XRP Ledger for tokenized funds supports the network's case for real-world finance, but the fund tokens don't require anyone to buy XRP, so the price link is indirect. XRP is still down about 14% over the past month, so this is a small bounce inside a larger slide.

outlook.bullCase: More tokenized-fund news and a steadier bitcoin above $80,000 could lift XRP back toward $1.40–$1.45.
outlook.bearCase: If bitcoin loses $80,000 again or the wider market turns risk-off after the Fed, XRP could slip back toward $1.20–$1.25.
outlook.watch: Whether Franklin clarifies who holds the new fund shares, bitcoin's hold on $80,000, and the Oct. 28 Fed decision.

crypto.name: Monero
crypto.why: Monero is the strongest large coin today, bouncing about 4.5% to roughly $608 while most of the top 20 sit flat or lower, as traders rotate into privacy coins (coins that hide who sent what to whom), a theme that has also lifted Zcash this week. It ran about 19% in the week to Oct. 22, briefly topping $650 for a nine-month high near $645, as futures bets rebuilt (open interest, the value of open futures contracts, rose about 22% in coin terms from Oct. 15 to Oct. 20, per Santiment data cited by The Crypto Times), then gave some of that back in Saturday's sell-off before today's rebound. Veteran trader Peter Brandt also drew attention by comparing its chart to silver's before its big run, though he gave no target.
crypto.meaning: Monero is moving on its own story rather than with bitcoin, which helps when the rest of the market is weak but also means sharp swings both ways. It remains about 23% below its January record near $799, and analysts at 24/7 Wall St. flag that the rising futures leverage looks like the build-up before its steep January drop.

outlook.bullCase: A close back above $650, the level that capped last week's rally, with privacy-coin demand holding up, could open a run toward $700 and later the $799 record.
outlook.bearCase: If leveraged bets unwind as they did in January, or bitcoin breaks lower, it could slip back under $580 and toward the mid-$500s where this month's rally began.
outlook.watch: The $650 level, futures open interest and funding rates, Zcash's moves (the two have traded together), and any exchange delisting or regulatory news on privacy coins.

crypto.name: Pepe
crypto.move: Down 2% in 24h, but up 12.7% this week, at about $0.0000044 (about flat over 30 days)
crypto.why: PEPE, the largest frog-themed meme coin (a token with no product, driven by online hype), is among the biggest gainers in the top 100 this week. There is no official news behind it: on Oct. 21 it had the biggest jump in trading activity on South Korean exchanges relative to normal, and futures trading has been running at more than five times spot trading, with open interest (the value of open bets) near $270 million, per CoinMarketCap's summary of market data. Early Friday CoinDesk flagged it up about 13%, its biggest gain among large coins in a month, as smaller coins bounced while bitcoin held steady. It has since given back all of that jump and more, and is down about 5% over 24 hours.
crypto.meaning: Gains built on borrowed money and a burst of retail trading in one region can unwind fast if those bets are closed. PEPE is still far below its December 2024 record, and meme coins tend to swing much more than bitcoin in both directions.

outlook.bullCase: If meme-coin interest keeps building and bitcoin holds $80,000, PEPE could extend toward the $0.0000055–$0.000006 area.
outlook.bearCase: A wider crypto sell-off or a wave of liquidations (leveraged bets closed automatically) could erase the week's gain and send it back toward $0.0000041–$0.0000044.
outlook.watch: Futures open interest and funding rates, Korean exchange volume, and whether bitcoin holds $80,000.

crypto.name: Aerodrome Finance
crypto.move: Down 5.9% in 24h, at about $0.682, now just outside the top 100 at No. 101 by market value (down about 18% this week)
crypto.why: Aerodrome, the biggest trading exchange on Coinbase's Base network, merged with its sister exchange Velodrome into a single platform called Aero, which went live on seven blockchains around Oct. 21–22. The token has fallen since in a classic 'sell the news' reaction: futures open interest (the value of open bets) dropped about 8% as traders cut leverage, and it broke below the $0.79–$0.80 support area that analysts had flagged.
crypto.meaning: The merger gives Aero a bigger footprint, but the market had priced it in, and old Velodrome holders received new AERO that some are selling. With the old support gone, swings are likely until the new token supply settles.

outlook.bullCase: Strong trading volume on the new multi-chain Aero and a quick reclaim of $0.79–$0.80 could carry it back toward $0.85–$0.90.
outlook.bearCase: Continued selling from converted Velodrome holders and a weak market could push it toward $0.65–$0.70.
outlook.watch: Daily trading volume and fees on Aero, whether it reclaims $0.80, and governance votes on emission (new token) rates.

crypto.name: AKEDO
crypto.move: Down 8.9% in 24h and 4.3% this week, at about $0.0290 (down 26% over 30 days)
crypto.why: AKEDO is a small AI-tools token that only just squeezed into CoinGecko's top 100. We could not find a clear news catalyst for its jump to about $0.039 late Friday, and that gain has now fully unwound: it has fallen about 24% from that peak to about $0.0295 (down about 10% on a rolling 24-hour basis), well below its old $0.037 ceiling and now slipping just under the $0.03 level we flagged. The slide comes days after a scheduled Oct. 21 unlock of tokens worth about $63 million (roughly 9% of its market value), and earlier community analysis found the top 100 wallets hold almost all of the supply, so a few holders can move the price sharply.
crypto.meaning: The failed breakout above $0.037 has turned into a slide of about a fifth, a reminder that a double-digit jump on no identifiable news, in a token with extremely concentrated ownership, can reverse quickly. Anyone holding it is exposed to large holders and freshly unlocked supply.

outlook.bullCase: Holding $0.03 and climbing back above the old $0.037 ceiling on steady volume would suggest the selling has run its course.
outlook.bearCase: A close below about $0.03 would open the way toward roughly $0.022, a level flagged as key support, especially if large holders or recipients of the Oct. 21 unlock keep selling.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds above about $0.03, trading volume, large-wallet transfers to exchanges, and any official project news.

crypto.name: NEAR Protocol
crypto.move: Down 4.8% in 24h and 10.7% this week, at about $4.41 (down 2% over 30 days)
crypto.why: NEAR, the token of a fast smart-contract blockchain (one that runs apps), is down about 4% over the past day at about $4.44, one of the weaker large coins this weekend. We could not find a fresh project-specific headline behind it; it looks like the same pattern seen across smaller coins this weekend, where traders using borrowed money get forced out as prices fall (a liquidation). The project is still carrying baggage from an Oct. 1 exploit that drained about $3.8 million from its NEAR Intents cross-chain service, which paused those services, per CoinDesk, and a whale's $2.6 million leveraged long was wiped out on Oct. 13 when it last tested this area.
crypto.meaning: NEAR has now slipped into the $4.40–$4.50 zone traders flagged as key support in mid-October, and it is down nearly 8% this week. Holders should expect sharp swings in thin weekend trading; the token tends to fall harder than bitcoin when the market turns cautious.

outlook.bullCase: If bitcoin steadies after next Wednesday's Fed decision and NEAR reclaims about $4.85–$5, the drop would look like a shake-out, opening a path back toward the mid-October highs above $5.
outlook.bearCase: A daily close well below $4.40–$4.50 would break the support analysts have watched since mid-October and could open a slide toward roughly $3.90–$4.
outlook.watch: Whether $4.40–$4.50 holds through the weekend, bitcoin's direction around $80,000, any update on the NEAR Intents exploit recovery, and futures liquidation data.

crypto.name: Zcash
crypto.move: Up 1.8% in 24h and 5.5% this week, at about $1,190 (down 23% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Traders had been positioning for the NU7 upgrade, which developers scheduled for about 7:50 p.m. ET on Nov. 5; it cuts block times from 75 to 25 seconds and sends 60% of fees to a reserve. Futures open interest (the value of open bets) had risen about 19–24% and two large traders reportedly opened about $37.6 million of 10x leveraged longs. Those leveraged bets have been unwinding: CoinDesk flagged ZEC among the coins where bullish traders were closing positions, and CoinDesk noted an 8% drop in open interest Friday, and after dipping below the $1,190–$1,230 support area, the price has bounced back into it, at about $1,203 (up about 3% on the day).
crypto.meaning: Much of this month's rally was driven by borrowed money, and this week shows how fast that can reverse. Upgrade dates often bring 'buy the rumour, sell the news' behaviour, so swings both ways are likely into Nov. 5.

outlook.bullCase: Holding the $1,180–$1,200 area and renewed interest as the upgrade nears could bring it back to the $1,375 resistance and, beyond that, the September high near $1,700.
outlook.bearCase: Losing $1,180 would erase the October breakout and could send it toward about $1,000–$1,120, near its 50-day average.
outlook.watch: The $1,180 level, funding rates and open interest, ETF flows, and any upgrade delay.

crypto.name: Solana
crypto.move: Down 0.5% in 24h and 2.1% this week, at about $101.60 (down 13% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Solana completed its Alpenglow upgrade, a major overhaul aimed at much faster transaction finality (the point at which a payment can't be reversed), according to CoinDesk. The price has moved with the market rather than rallying on the news, and it slipped under $100 Saturday morning as bitcoin's break below $80,000 triggered forced selling across crypto, before recovering to about $101.80.
crypto.meaning: A smooth Alpenglow launch is a meaningful technical milestone, but the market is treating it as already expected. The first days after a big upgrade are when problems usually show up, so stability matters more than headlines.

outlook.bullCase: A trouble-free upgrade and stronger crypto risk appetite could lift SOL back toward $115–$120.
outlook.bearCase: Any outage or bug after the upgrade, or bitcoin staying below $80,000, could push SOL toward $90.
outlook.watch: Whether SOL regains $100, network stability after Alpenglow, bitcoin's $80,000 level, and Solana ETF flows.

stocks.name: S&P 500
stocks.move: Closed down 0.5% (40 points) at 7,624, its second straight weekly loss; about 2.8% below its record near 7,845
stocks.why: Oil and yields back near 5% weighed on the index, and nearly three in four S&P 500 stocks fell, per AP. Banks, telecoms, industrials and consumer names led the decline while energy (ConocoPhillips up 3.6%, Chevron up 2.9%) and chips gained; the University of Michigan's final October consumer sentiment reading slipped to 48.0, near a record low, with year-ahead inflation expectations at 4.7%.
stocks.meaning: The damage is concentrated in tech, which makes up a large share of the index, while other sectors are holding up better. Falling bond yields help a little, but a 10-year yield near 5% still makes stocks look expensive relative to bonds.

outlook.bullCase: Solid results from Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon next week, a calm Fed on Oct. 28 and yields easing further could carry it back toward the 7,845 record.
outlook.bearCase: A deeper tech sell-off, a hawkish Fed, or an oil spike above $115 could drag it below 7,600 toward the 7,500 area.
outlook.watch: Whether 7,600 holds early next week, oil prices, and the Fed decision on Oct. 28 followed by Microsoft and Alphabet earnings that evening.

outlook.bearCase: If selling resumes, the 25,800–25,900 area could give way, with the 25,500 area the next stop; disappointing cloud results next week would add pressure.

stocks.name: S&P/TSX Composite
stocks.move: Closed down 0.5% (185 points) at 35,788 after being down 1.3% earlier; about 3.5% below its high
stocks.why: Toronto slipped with Wall Street on AI-spending worries and higher energy costs, per The Canadian Press. Banks eased (RBC and TD each down about 0.4%) and gold fell 1.2% to about $4,008, hitting miners, while oil producers were the bright spot, with Canadian Natural up 2.1% to a record close as U.S. crude rose to about $103.30.
stocks.meaning: High oil prices support Canada's energy producers, but the TSX's heavy weighting in miners makes it sensitive to falling gold, and a likely Bank of Canada hike next week could weigh on rate-sensitive stocks. Friday's strong retail sales (up 1.2% in August) and a rising loonie point to an economy holding up better than feared.

outlook.bullCase: Oil holding near $100, a Bank of Canada decision that signals no more hikes after this one, and continued bank strength could take the TSX back toward its 37,000 high.
outlook.bearCase: A drop in oil on an Iran deal, a Bank of Canada that hints at several hikes, or a hawkish Fed lifting yields could pull it back toward 35,500.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.move: Closed down 1.0% at about $642.60, after Thursday's 7% drop; it touched $633 early Friday
stocks.why: Third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, beating forecasts, and fourth-quarter guidance topped estimates, but the stock fell as investors focus on costs: Meta expects $135–$145 billion of capital spending, free cash flow was about -$2.1 billion this quarter, and a $9.9 billion legal charge cut reported profit. It also surprised Wall Street with a new non-voting Class C share, one for every share held starting in January 2027; JPMorgan's Doug Anmuth called the pending shares an overhang (a supply worry hanging over the price) and urged Meta to issue any new stock quickly. Meta's filing says the Class C dividend is expected to work like a two-for-one stock split for Class A holders.
stocks.meaning: The core ad business is growing fast, which supports the stock, but AI spending pushed free cash flow negative (about -$2.1 billion) this quarter. A separate $25 billion penalty imposed by a New Mexico judge in a privacy case is under appeal and adds legal uncertainty.

outlook.bullCase: At least 13 brokerages raised price targets after the results, per LSEG; if buyers return to the strong ad growth, it could recover toward the $700 level.
outlook.bearCase: Worry about open-ended AI spending, a share sale to fund it, or the $25 billion New Mexico penalty could push it below Thursday's low near $640 toward the $620–$630 area.
outlook.watch: Whether Thursday's low near $640 holds, any details on Class C share issuance, and Alphabet's and Microsoft's spending plans on Oct. 28.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices
stocks.move: Closed up 1.7% at about $516.80, rebounding after Thursday's 8.1% drop
stocks.why: There is no AMD-specific news; it fell Thursday in a broad AI-chip sell-off as Meta's spending plans and a report that Nvidia and Tesla will invest $2.8 billion in Samsung Electro-Mechanics revived worries about 'circular' financing, where chip buyers and sellers fund each other, and it bounced Friday as that selling faded. AMD also trades at a high valuation, about 200 times its past year's earnings, which leaves little room for disappointment.
stocks.meaning: AMD has been one of the biggest AI winners of the past year, more than doubling from its low, so it swings hard when sentiment turns. Its own results on Nov. 3 are the next real test of whether AI chip demand is holding up.

outlook.bullCase: Strong Microsoft and Alphabet spending plans on Oct. 28 and solid guidance on Nov. 3 could lift it back toward $560–$600.
outlook.bearCase: If the AI-spending worry deepens, it could slide toward the $470–$480 area where it traded in late September.
outlook.watch: Chip-sector moves, Big Tech capital-spending guidance on Oct. 28–29, and AMD's Nov. 3 results.

stocks.name: American Express
stocks.move: Closed down 3.7% Friday after third-quarter results
stocks.why: American Express beat profit forecasts: adjusted earnings were $4.68 a share versus about $4.48 expected, and revenue rose 9% to $20.1 billion, roughly in line. It raised its 2026 adjusted profit forecast to $17.60–$17.90 a share and said it will cut about 5% of its global workforce. Shares still slipped because card spending volumes came in slightly below estimates, with total network volume of $517.9 billion against about $519.5 billion expected.
stocks.meaning: The results show wealthier card users are still spending, especially on travel, which is a decent sign for the consumer economy. But the stock often falls after good reports (Truist notes this would be its ninth drop in 11 quarters after a beat), so expectations were already high.

outlook.bullCase: If investors focus on the raised forecast and cost cuts, the stock could recover and test resistance near $327.
outlook.bearCase: Further worry about slowing spending growth or a weaker consumer, as oil prices squeeze budgets, could keep it under pressure.
outlook.watch: Whether it stabilizes next week, card-spending trends in other lenders' results, and U.S. consumer sentiment and jobs data.

stocks.move: Closed down 0.6% at about $211, after Thursday's 4.4% drop; about 13% below its 52-week high
stocks.why: Nvidia fell with the chip sector Thursday as Meta's spending plans revived questions about AI returns, and it did not join Friday's chip bounce. A Korean newspaper report that Nvidia and Tesla plan to invest $2.8 billion in Samsung Electro-Mechanics added to 'circular financing' worries, and Microsoft said Friday it plans to use its own Maia chips for AI inference, though Bloomberg Intelligence says they lag Nvidia's.
stocks.meaning: Nvidia is the core of the AI trade and a large part of the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, so its direction matters for most index funds. Big Tech customers' spending plans next week are the main near-term signal for its sales.

outlook.bullCase: Higher spending plans from Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon on Oct. 28–29 could lift it back toward $230–$240.
outlook.bearCase: Spending cuts or more 'circular financing' headlines could push it toward the $200–$205 area; it is already near the low end of its past month's range.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.move: Closed down 0.6% at about $372, after touching $365 early; down 3.1% Thursday
stocks.why: Tesla rose during the day on Musk's comments that Tesla and SpaceX formed committees to study a merger. After the close it reported adjusted earnings of $0.48 a share versus about $0.45 expected and revenue of $28.05 billion, flat from a year ago and slightly below some forecasts; free cash flow of $1.5 billion beat expectations of a cash burn because spending came in about $3 billion lower than expected. Shares fell about 5% before the open as Tesla cut its 2026 capital-spending plan to about $20 billion from more than $25 billion and Musk said reaching 20,000 Optimus robots a week will take at least a year. Buyers erased the early loss after the open, but it slipped again as the Nasdaq weakened and closed near the day's low.
stocks.meaning: The core business is weak: operating income fell 56% to $718 million and deliveries slipped 2%, so the stock still trades mostly on robotaxi, Optimus and SpaceX-merger hopes. Lower spending helps cash flow but can read as a slower AI push, which explains the early selling.

outlook.bullCase: Concrete merger progress or a smooth Cybercab expansion to Dallas next month could bring it back toward $400–$410.
outlook.bearCase: If the early dip resumes and analysts trim targets, it could slide back toward $355–$375.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds the $365 area, merger committee news, and the NHTSA Cybercab response due Oct. 30.

stocks.name: TD Bank
stocks.move: Closed down 0.4% at about C$174.47, a day after closing near its record of C$175.99
stocks.why: Canadian banks were among the TSX laggards Friday (RBC also fell about 0.4%), giving back some of their recent strength as oil and yields climb. Markets see about an 80% chance the Bank of Canada raises its rate to 2.50% on Oct. 28; a modest hike tends to help bank lending margins, while several hikes would raise worries about mortgage holders and loan losses.

outlook.bearCase: A Bank of Canada that signals several hikes, raising fears for mortgage holders and loan losses, could pull it back to the C$167–C$170 area.
outlook.watch: The Bank of Canada decision and Monetary Policy Report on Oct. 28.

newCoins.name: Irys
newCoins.what: A young 'datachain' blockchain (launched about a year ago) that combines on-chain data storage with smart contracts and pitches itself to AI-data apps; IRYS pays fees and is staked by validators.
newCoins.why: It is the top trending coin on CoinGecko after one of the wildest swings of the month: it jumped more than tenfold in a day to a record near $0.30–$0.33 on Thursday evening (ET), then lost roughly three-quarters of that within hours and is now around $0.043, down about 51% in 24 hours. No outlet found a confirmed cause; the run looked like a short squeeze (traders betting on a fall being forced to buy back), with about $21 million of short positions liquidated.
newCoins.redFlags: Only about 20% of the 10 billion tokens circulate, with team and investor tokens due to start unlocking after the first year. Futures open interest (about $1.2 billion at the peak) was many times its market value, so leverage, not buyers, drove the price, and price feeds disagree sharply on where it trades.
